summary: Full-stack testing of SesDeşifre (Turkish audio → text with OpenAI Whisper). Backend: 8/8 pytest tests passed including a REAL Whisper transcription of a JFK-style WAV that returned meaningful text. Frontend: dropzone, upload, progress bar, result panel, copy, download and reset flows all work end-to-end via Playwright with data-testid selectors. One real bug found: backend advertises .flac and .ogg support but the underlying emergentintegrations Whisper wrapper only supports mp3/mp4/mpeg/mpga/m4a/wav/webm — uploading .flac/.ogg returns HTTP 500 with a leaky provider error string.

critical.issue: ALLOWED_EXTS advertises 'flac' and 'ogg' (server.py L28) but the Whisper wrapper rejects them ⇒ 500 'Transkripsiyon başarısız: Validation error: Unsupported file format: flac. Supported formats: mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, wav, webm'. UI also shows these as accepted formats. Fix: either drop flac/ogg from ALLOWED_EXTS (backend + frontend + dropzone chip + accept attr) OR transcode server-side.

minor.issue: Provider validation errors are surfaced to the user unmodified in Turkish UI (leaks internal error text). Consider mapping provider validation errors to a friendlier Turkish 400 message before returning.

integration_issues.issue: Dropzone chip in Transcriber.jsx (L244) shows 'mp3 · wav · m4a · ogg · flac · webm' and ALLOWED_EXT (L20) accepts .ogg/.flac, but backend will 500 on those. User will experience opaque error after a full upload.

action_items: Decide flac/ogg policy: remove them from backend ALLOWED_EXTS (server.py) AND from frontend ALLOWED_EXT + dropzone hint + <input accept=…> in Transcriber.jsx, OR add server-side transcoding to wav before calling Whisper.
Wrap provider errors in a friendlier Turkish 400 for unsupported-by-provider formats instead of a raw 500 with provider text.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py ALLOWED_EXTS is inconsistent with the actual Whisper-supported list — this is the root cause of the flac/ogg failure.
server.py catches generic Exception and returns 500 with str(e). This leaks provider internals into the client; should map known provider messages to 4xx.
Transcriber.jsx: ALLOWED_EXT constant is duplicated across the frontend (constant, accept attr, dropzone hint string) — move to a single source of truth.
server.py line 108: 'if language and 2 <= len(language) <= 5' then slices to [:2]. Bounds check is loose; OK for MVP but consider strict ISO-639-1 whitelist.
Frontend progress bar goes 0→70 during upload and jumps to 95→100 after the network completes; there is no genuine processing progress. Acceptable for MVP but user may perceive a stall at 70%.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suite at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py — 8 tests, ~5s runtime, includes REAL Whisper call on /app/test_fixtures/jfk.wav (expects English words dark/suit/greasy/etc.). If main agent removes flac/ogg from ALLOWED_EXTS, update TestTranscribeReal.test_transcribe_flac_reports_error_gracefully to expect 400 instead of 500. Fixtures live in /app/test_fixtures. EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is set in /app/backend/.env.
rca_of_the_issue: server.py ALLOWED_EXTS = {mp3, wav, m4a, ogg, flac, webm, mp4, mpeg, mpga}. emergentintegrations.llm.openai.OpenAISpeechToText.transcribe() performs its own extension validation with only {mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, wav, webm}. Reproduction: `curl -F file=@sample.flac -F language=en $URL/api/transcribe` → 500 with detail containing 'Unsupported file format: flac'. Mitigation: (a) remove flac & ogg from both server ALLOWED_EXTS and frontend ALLOWED_EXT/accept/dropzone; (b) or transcode via pydub/ffmpeg on backend before invoking Whisper.
